review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: It is often believed that students who have the best result should be rewarded, while some people argue that it is more important to reward those students who show improvements. In my view, both these types of students should be rewarded equally.

Admittedly, it is right to reward students who show the best result. Initially, students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and even others to study harder so win the rewards, leading to propel towards overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of live. Studying in an environment where only the best individuals are rewarded, students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which can enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, I believe students who show their improvements also worth receiving rewards. Since if only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, it can cause others to think that their effort is futile because of can not surpassing those outstanding individuals. As a result, it can make students to prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened which make them gradually lose the incentive to study. Conversely, emphasizing improvements can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and also help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves by irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Therefore, the constant desire to outdo themselves and even benefit them more than competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I believe that whether the students show the highest result or their improvements, both should be rewarded equally.

Hai đoạn thân bài giữ được đủ các chuỗi ý Cô giao: nỗ lực được ghi nhận, cạnh tranh chuẩn bị cho tương lai, và việc chỉ thưởng số ít có thể làm các em khác nản chí. paragraphs: It is often argued by many people that public museums and art galleries are increasing lose its importance now since viewers can see historical objects and works of art by using a computer. I disagree with this view since public museums and art galleries still have vituals values in daily life, though the fact that Internet have some irrefutable impacts.

Admittedly, technology can bring individuals beneficial and convenient experiences about art and history. Things such as high-resolution images, three dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms that can enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable details without living home. For example, Louvre museum in Paris offers online collection in order to help people all around the world who cannot afford or have mobility issues still have chance to access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries are still necessary. Initially, online experiences cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artwork in persons, since this activity can evoke viewers' emotions and sense of authenticity which digital images cannot convey. This can seen in the way people directly enjoy historical objects in museum such as a soldier uniforms, a old gun or a flag. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region because of they can be a magnet for tourism and a facilitator of bonding within the community.

In conclusion, technology can help people enjoy masterpieces or artefacts more easily; however, public museums and art galleries still have many irrefutable importance that cannot seen without enjoying in-person.

Nhưng các khung nền đã học chưa được tự soát: “Things such as ... that can enable” là mảnh câu thiếu động từ chính; “because of they can be” sai cấu trúc và đảo chiều nguyên nhân–hệ quả; kết bài “cannot seen” thiếu be. Ngay ý ở mở bài cũng làm nhẹ dự đoán của đề. Bài còn ẩu ở khâu kiểm câu hoàn chỉnh. Em cần nghiêm túc, cầu thị sửa từng câu được đánh dấu, giải thích vì sao hiện vật thật gợi cảm xúc rồi tự kiểm lại chủ ngữ–động từ trước khi nộp.

paragraphs: It is often argued that public museums and art galleries will become unnecessary since viewers can see historical objects and works of art on a computer. I am of the opposite school of thought since public museums and art galleries still have vital value in daily life, despite the benefits of the Internet.

Admittedly, technology can bring individuals beneficial and convenient experiences of art and history. High-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms can enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. For example, Louvre museum in Paris offers an online collection to help people around the world who cannot afford museum visits or have mobility issues access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries are still necessary. Initially, online experiences cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artwork in person, since this activity can evoke viewers' emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. This can be seen when people directly view historical objects in a museum, such as a soldier's uniform, an old gun or a flag; seeing them in person can make the history of war feel more immediate. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. This role makes them magnets for tourism and facilitators of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, technology can help people enjoy masterpieces or artefacts more easily; however, public museums and art galleries remain important for the in-person experiences they offer.

paragraphs: It is often believed that dangerous sports must be prohibited by law while others think individuals should be free to take part. I am personally of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that government should ban dangerous sports since even a minor error can cause the death of a participant. For example, if a person take part in skydiving without preparing carefully, they may lose control and face to danger. However, I think the prohibition in dangerous sports are not practical. While most kinds of these sports happen in remote locations, say, mountain cliffs, where have minimal surveillance and control. It is also unrealistic for a police officer to follow every individuals in order to make sure that nobody can do such activities. As a result, a prohibition can exist only on paper and even make things become worse if people try driving practice underground which create more difficulties to ensure basic safety standards.

To add further credence to my assertion, I note people are permitted to do any sports, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. Specifically, individuals can join in many reputable clubs as deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping where provide appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Moreover, new participants can be accompanied by an expert and being taught about dangers and respond appropriately. I believe proper training and necessary precautions can [chưa đọc rõ] safer participation; however, no activity entirely risk-free.

In conclusion, from my perspective, banning neither practical nor effective. Instead, people have freedom to choose any sports with receiving strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: It is often believed that dangerous sports must be prohibited by law while others think individuals should be free to take part. I am personally of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that the government should ban dangerous sports since even a minor error can cause the death of a participant. For example, if a person takes part in skydiving without preparing carefully, they may lose control and face danger. However, I think a prohibition on dangerous sports is not practical. Many of these sports take place in remote locations, say, mountain cliffs, where surveillance and control are minimal. In addition, it is unrealistic for a police officer to follow every individual to make sure that nobody can do such activities. As a result, a prohibition can exist only on paper and may even make things worse by driving the practice underground, which makes it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

To add further credence to my assertion, I note people should be permitted to do any sports, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. Specifically, individuals interested in deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping can join reputable clubs that provide appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Moreover, new participants can be accompanied by an expert and taught how to recognise dangers and respond appropriately. I believe proper training and necessary precautions can make participation safer; however, no activity is entirely risk-free.

In conclusion, from my perspective, banning is neither practical nor effective. Instead, allowing people to choose any sport under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.
The graph below shows the three different kinds of emission sources (oil/coal/gas) of greenhouse gas in the UK.
Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
Write at least 150 words.

paragraphs: The given bar chart illustrates how much three different kinds of emission sources (oil / coal / gas) of greenhouse gas in the UK was over a 20-year period, commencing from 1990.

Overall, there was an increase was seen in the figure for Gas while the opposite trend was true for coal. Also of note is that oil experienced some insignificant changes throughout the surveyed years.

To elaborate, in 1990, gas ranked the bottom among three studied objects with a mere 220 million tons before growing stably over the period to reach the peak by over 300 million tons in 2010. Conversely, the figure for coal was approximately 305 million tons in the first year; however it witnessed a sharp decline over the years and got only nearly 200 million tons, marking the lowest point of the entire chart.

Regarding the remaining object, the figure for oil in the 1990 was noticeable by 270 million tons. This data went down slightly for the first five-year period then increased by a mere 20 millions tons in 1995 before decreasing for the remaining period to got over 200 millions in the last surveyed year.
review.overall: Em đã nhận ra gas tăng, coal giảm và gas từ mức thấp nhất trở thành nhóm cao nhất; cách tách gas/coal rồi oil có thể dùng được. Tuy nhiên, overview nói oil chỉ thay đổi không đáng kể trong khi cột này giảm khá rõ từ đầu đến cuối, và em đặt mức hồi phục của oil vào năm 1995 thay vì 2000. Mở bài chưa nêu đúng đại lượng khí thải, còn vài câu dùng hai động từ chồng nhau hoặc chọn sai cấu trúc đi với số liệu. Em hãy kiểm lại từng mốc trước khi chốt xu hướng chung.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart shows how much greenhouse gas was emitted from oil, coal and gas in the UK between 1990 and 2010. The amounts are given in millions of tons at five-year intervals.

Overall, gas emissions increased throughout the period and became the highest of the three by 2000, while coal emissions fell steadily. Oil emissions also declined from the first to the last year, although they recovered briefly after 1995.

In 1990, gas-related emissions were the lowest, at about 220 million tons, compared with around 270 million tons for oil and 310 million tons for coal. The gas figure rose at every displayed point, reaching a peak of about 320 million tons in 2010. Coal followed the opposite pattern: its figure fell from approximately 310 million tons in 1990 to about 250 million in 2000 and then to nearly 200 million in 2010, the lowest value on the chart.

Regarding the remaining fuel, oil emissions stood at around 270 million tons in 1990. The figure dropped to about 240 million in 1995 before rising by roughly 20 million tons to 260 million in 2000. It then decreased during the rest of the period, ending at just over 200 million tons in 2010. Thus, despite its temporary rise, oil recorded a net fall over the two decades.

task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: It is often argued that history is one of the most important subjects at school while others believe that subjects like science and technology have more benefits than history in today's world. I agree with the second argument while acknowledge that history still has some advantages for nowadays.

Admittedly, history is an important subject at school, even is real life. For individuals, history helps them understand about the starting and history of their countries and the world, which can broaden their horizon and also teach them good personalities such as brave or hard-working through the historical wars. Moreover, history also related to many jobs in real life such as teacher or architect, that kinds of jobs require people to have a large knowledge and experiments about history. This can answer why in some nations such as Viet Nam, history is still a main subject for students in lower primary and secondary.

However, in modern and developing life now, I believe that subjects like science and technology have much more advantages in today's world. This can be explained by that technology appears in every categories in daily life while history doesn't since science and technology still increasingly developing everyday. For example, in the past, students have to study in traditional classes but now, we can learn through the Internet thanks to science, which make studying become more convenient.
review.overall: Em trả lời đủ hai luồng ý và nêu quan điểm rõ: khoa học–công nghệ quan trọng hơn hiện nay nhưng lịch sử vẫn có ích. Ví dụ học qua Internet giúp đoạn thứ ba có điểm tựa cụ thể. Tuy nhiên, nhiều lập luận còn nhảy bước, nhất là từ học lịch sử sang nghề kiến trúc và từ 'technology appears everywhere' sang kết luận so sánh. Bài dừng sau đoạn khoa học và chưa có kết luận; em nên hoàn thiện một câu kết ngắn, đồng thời sửa các cấu trúc như 'while acknowledge' và 'which make'.

criteria.comment: Em bàn đến lợi ích của lịch sử và lợi ích của khoa học–công nghệ, đồng thời giữ quan điểm ưu tiên nhóm thứ hai trong mở và thân bài. Ví dụ học trực tuyến có liên quan, nhưng giải thích so sánh còn rộng và ý nghề nghiệp của lịch sử thiếu bước nối; bài chưa có kết luận.

criteria.comment: Ba đoạn có tiến trình dễ theo: lập trường, nhượng bộ cho lịch sử, rồi lý do ưu tiên khoa học–công nghệ. Admittedly/However dùng đúng quan hệ, nhưng câu lịch sử dồn nhiều ý và thiếu đoạn kết để khép lập luận.

criteria.label: Lexical Resource

paragraphs.text: Some people place history among the most valuable subjects taught at school, whereas others believe science and technology are more important today. I agree with the second view because these subjects have a wider range of practical uses, although history also gives students knowledge that matters.

Admittedly, studying history helps young people understand how their country and other societies developed. Learning about past conflicts and decisions may help them appreciate their culture and reflect on qualities such as bravery and perseverance. Historical knowledge can also support particular careers. A history teacher, for example, needs to explain the causes and effects of events, while an architect restoring an old building may need to understand its original purpose. These are valuable uses of history, even if they do not apply to every occupation.

However, science and technology are increasingly useful in many parts of daily life, including education and communication. In the past, students usually had to attend lessons in a classroom, but internet access now allows many of them to review materials or speak with a teacher from home. This does not mean that classroom teaching is unnecessary; it means technology offers another way to study when travel or time is a problem. Scientific knowledge also helps people evaluate information and make informed decisions about new tools. Because these skills can be applied in a broad range of situations, I consider science and technology particularly important in the modern world.

In conclusion, history is worth studying for its cultural and professional benefits. Nevertheless, I would give greater priority to science and technology because their practical applications affect more aspects of students' present and future lives.
